name: phd-nd-masters-then-phd
description: A Ph.D. student who did their bachelor's AND their MSCSE at Notre Dame, then entered the Ph.D. (DGS 2026-09-09). One Notre Dame transcript covers all three careers, split at the entry term: the undergraduate courses satisfy §4.4.1 core knowledge but never transfer (§5.2 criterion 2); the MSCSE courses count in full toward the Ph.D. WITHOUT transfer approval and beyond §5.2's cap (Graduate School through the DGS, 2026-09-22: "in cases where a graduate student moves from a master's program to a PhD program in the same discipline all the credits are counted towards the PhD, even those above and beyond the usual 24 allowed for transfer" — until then they were §5.2 transfer candidates); the MSCSE thesis-direction credits count toward the total only (DGS 2026-09-22), the courses satisfy §4.4.2, and the §4.5 along-the-way MSCSE row is left out for a student who already holds the degree. Since the courses are not transfer credit, the §5.2 row has nothing to list and says so.

detailIncludes: Your Notre Dame MSCSE coursework (CSE 60641, CSE 60111, CSE 60321, CSE 68901) is not transfer credit

CSE 30321: not eligible for degree credit at the 30000-level — only CSE 40000-level courses
CSE 68901: counts toward the total-credit requirement only (6 cr)
from your Notre Dame MSCSE — counts in full toward the Ph.D. without transfer approval
a master’s project or thesis is not a regular course, so it counts toward the total credits only (§4.2)
